# Capstone build spec: the kitchen-sink Tour of Heroes This is the conformance target for the capstone build. It is intent plus decisions, not pixels: a low-fidelity layout, build guidelines, a theme palette, and an icon scheme. Build to this with the real sealed spartan primitives and the MVVM pattern, under all gates. Do NOT chase a pixel-perfect mock. `prototype/tour-of-heroes.html` is a colour-and-mood reference ONLY. It is known to be non-responsive (measured: 19 responsive-gate violations) and its CSS and layout mechanics must not be copied. Take the look and feel from it; take the structure, palette, icons, and responsive rules from this document. ## How to use this - The app is "Hero Ops Console": Tour of Heroes reimagined as a superhero agency's mission control. That framing is what makes the kitchen sink coherent (a roster, missions, threats, recruiting) rather than a component zoo. - Build every screen responsive-correct at 375px, 768px, and 1280px. The Part 5 responsive gate is on: no horizontal page scroll, no element escaping the viewport, no clipped content at any of the three widths. This is the bar the mock failed and the build must clear. - Use spartan primitives for everything that has one. Compose, do not hand-roll. The sealing gate enforces this once the vocabulary is expanded. ## Theme palette A cool indigo-biased neutral set with an amber-gold action colour and a permanently-dark navigation rail. Apply these to the existing spartan CSS tokens in `src/styles.css` (the `:root` and `:root.dark` blocks). Names below are roles; map each to spartan's own token (for example the action colour is spartan's `--primary`, the subtle hover background is spartan's `--accent`, which is a different thing; do not confuse the two). ``` role light dark ---- ----- ---- action / primary #d8891a #f5b843 on-primary #ffffff #241a05 page background #f6f7fa #0e1018 foreground (text) #1b1e2b #eceef6 card / popover #ffffff #171a26 muted surface #eef0f6 #1e2231 muted foreground #5b6072 #9aa0b4 border / input #e4e7ef #272b3b focus ring amber @ 35% amber @ 40% --- navigation rail (dark in both themes) --- sidebar background #1e2233 #10121c sidebar foreground #eceef6 #eceef6 sidebar muted #9aa0b4 #8b90a6 sidebar active bg #2a2f45 #20263c --- semantic (separate from the accent; these carry meaning) --- success (Active) #2fb574 #3ecb84 warning (Injured) #e4802b #f0983f destructive (MIA/retire) #e5484d #f2585d info #4f7cf0 #6f97f6 ``` Radius: cards and controls around 9-10px, dialogs a touch larger. Elevation is restrained: one soft shadow on cards, a stronger one only on popovers and dialogs. Do not stamp the same shadow and radius on every block. Theme switch is a `.dark` class toggled on `` (the substrate already defines `:root` and `:root.dark`). Persist the choice; respect `prefers-color-scheme` when the user has made no choice. ## Icon scheme Icons are `@ng-icons/core` with the lucide set (`@ng-icons/lucide`), registered per component with `provideIcons({ ... })` and rendered as ``. There is no `hlm-icon` wrapper. Raw inline `
Hero Ops
Operations
  • Dashboard
  • Roster
  • Missions
  • Threats
  • Recruit
  • Settings

Base directory for this skill: D:\Repos\angular-jig\.claude\skills\house-style # House frontend conventions These are this repo's conventions, layered on top of the SpartanNG docs (the `spartan` skill). They extend the spartan docs where spartan is silent; they never contradict them. Where spartan already has a rule (semantic colors, `class` is for layout only, `gap-*` not `space-*`, `size-*` for equal dimensions), follow the spartan skill; this file adds only what spartan does not cover. One deliberate exception: spartan's examples put Tailwind utilities in the template's `class` attribute. In this repo they never go there; see "Markup is BEM, styling lives in the stylesheet" below. Every other spartan rule stands, including "class is for layout only" on a primitive, which now means the utilities a primitive's BEM class applies must be layout only. ## Markup is BEM, styling lives in the stylesheet A template says what things are; the stylesheet says how they look. Utility classes in markup turn every template into a wall of `flex items-center gap-3 sm:w-48` that a reader has to decode to find the structure, and they let styling decisions spread across every file that renders the element. So: 1. **Template classes are BEM names only.** Every token in a `class` attribute, every `[class.x]` binding, and every string inside a `[class]` binding is `block`, `block__element`, `block--modifier` or `block__element--modifier`, lowercase kebab-case. No Tailwind utility appears in a template. That includes `sr-only`: write `class="roster__label"` and `@apply sr-only` it. 2. **One block per component, named after the component file.** `hero-card.ts` owns `.hero-card`, `.hero-card__name`, `.hero-card--retired`, and nothing else. A template must not use another component's block, and a stylesheet must not define one. `:host` is allowed. 3. **Every component is three files.** `hero-card.ts` with `templateUrl: './hero-card.html'` and `styleUrl: './hero-card.css'`. Never `template:` or `styles:`, however small the component. `ng g component` already produces this shape. 4. **Stylesheets are plain `.css` with every BEM class written out in full.** Not `.scss`: Tailwind v4 does not support running behind Sass. The first line is always `@reference "../../styles.css";` (adjust the `../` count to the file's depth under `src/app`), which lets `@apply` resolve the theme's tokens and variants. Write `.roster__row { ... }`, never `.roster { &__row { ... } }`: that is Sass syntax, and native CSS compiles it to a selector that matches nothing, with only a warning. Nesting is fine for states and breakpoints on the same element: `&:hover`, `&::before`, `&[aria-expanded="true"]`, `@media`. 5. **App stylesheets are layout only.** Every utility in `@apply` and every plain declaration in a stylesheet under `src/app`, and every class rule in `src/styles.css`, must be layout: display, flex and grid arrangement, gap, sizing, margin, position, overflow and text alignment (the full list is under "The layout list" below). Color, typography, border, radius, shadow, ring, opacity, transitions, cursor, custom properties and anything not on the list are appearance, and appearance lives in `libs/ui`. Padding is allowed in one place: the component's block root (`.roster`, `.roster--compact`, or `:host`), for the region's inset, and only when that element is not a primitive. Semantic tokens only, `gap-*` not `space-*`, grid for regions. Moving appearance onto a wrapper element, or removing a primitive's directive to keep its look, does not make it allowed. 6. **No utility classes in TypeScript.** No `cva` variant strings, no `host: { class: '...' }`, no computed class strings. A state that changes appearance is a BEM modifier bound with `[class.block--modifier]`. Never build a class name from data (`roster__row--{{ hero.status }}`): write one modifier per state and bind each with `[class.roster__row--active]`, so every class a template can carry is written out in full. Helm directives and their inputs are not classes and stay in the template: `variant`, `size` and the directive itself are the primitive's API. ```html

Roster

Every hero on the books.

Recruit
@for (hero of vm.heroes(); track hero.id) {
{{ hero.name }} @if (hero.retired) { Retired }
}
``` ```css /* roster.css */ @reference "../../styles.css"; .roster { @apply grid gap-6 p-6; } .roster__header { @apply grid gap-1; } .roster__filters { @apply flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3; } .roster__label { @apply sr-only; } .roster__search { @apply w-full sm:w-64; } .roster__recruit { @apply ms-auto; } .roster__row { @apply flex items-center gap-2; } ``` Note what the stylesheet does not say. No rule picks a color, a font size, a weight or a radius: the title is `hlmH3`, the caption `hlmMuted`, the icon's color its `tone`, the retired state a badge variant. `p-6` sits on `.roster`, the block root, as the region's inset. `roster__search` and `roster__recruit` sit on primitives and apply only width and margin. When no existing variant gives the look you need (an input padded to make room for an icon, a quieter table cell, a rounded panel), add a variant to the primitive itself: edit the owned copy of its component in `libs/ui`, add the variant to its `cva` using semantic tokens only, and select it from the template with the input (``). `libs/ui` is the one place `cva` and utility strings in TypeScript belong; rule 6 applies to `src/app`. One variant serves every screen that needs the look, which is the point: a primitive's appearance is decided in one place, not re-decided at every call site. ### The layout list After any variant prefix (`sm:`, `hover:`, `dark:`) and a `!` marker are removed, these are layout. Anything else is appearance. - Display and box: `block`, `inline`, `inline-block`, `flex`, `inline-flex`, `grid`, `inline-grid`, `contents`, `hidden`, `sr-only`, `not-sr-only`, `box-border`, `box-content`. - Flex and grid: `flex-*`, `grow*`, `shrink*`, `basis-*`, `order-*`, `grid-cols-*`, `grid-rows-*`, `col-*`, `row-*`, `auto-cols-*`, `auto-rows-*`, `grid-flow-*`, `items-*`, `justify-*`, `content-*` (alignment), `self-*`, `place-*`, `gap-*`. - Sizing: `w-*`, `h-*`, `size-*`, `min-w-*`, `min-h-*`, `max-w-*`, `max-h-*`, `aspect-*`. - Margin: `m-*`, `mx-*`, `my-*`, `mt-*`, `mr-*`, `mb-*`, `ml-*`, `ms-*`, `me-*`, and negatives. - Position: `static`, `relative`, `absolute`, `fixed`, `sticky`, `inset-*`, `top-*`, `right-*`, `bottom-*`, `left-*`, `start-*`, `end-*`, `z-*`. - Overflow and flow: `overflow-*`, `overscroll-*`, `truncate`, `text-ellipsis`, `text-clip`, `whitespace-*`, `break-*`, `text-left`, `text-center`, `text-right`, `text-start`, `text-end`, `text-justify`, `object-*`, `isolate`, `container`. - Padding: only on the block root. Plain declarations follow the same line: `display`, `flex*`, `grid*`, `gap`, sizing, `margin*`, `position`, `inset*`, `top`/`right`/`bottom`/`left`, `z-index`, `overflow*`, `text-overflow`, `white-space`, `word-break`, `overflow-wrap`, `text-align`, `object-fit`, `object-position`, `isolation`, `order`, `align-*`, `justify-*`, `place-*`. `color: var(--sidebar-primary)` is appearance. ### Where appearance comes from - **A primitive's look:** its `variant`/`size` inputs; when none fits, a new variant on the primitive in `libs/ui` (above). - **Text:** a typography directive from `@spartan-ng/helm/typography`: `hlmH1` to `hlmH4`, `hlmP`, `hlmLead`, `hlmLarge`, `hlmSmall`, `hlmMuted`, `hlmCode`, `hlmBlockquote`, `hlmUl`. `

{{ hint }}

`, not `

` with `text-sm text-muted-foreground`. When none fits (a stat value, an emphasized table number), add a variant to the closest one in `libs/ui/typography`. - **Icon color:** `` from `@spartan-ng/helm/icon`. Tones: `default` (inherits the surrounding color), `muted`, `primary`, `destructive`, `success`, `warning`. Size icons with `ng-icon`'s `size` input or `size-*` in the stylesheet. - **A region's inset:** padding on the block root. - **Status colors:** `success` and `warning` exist as tokens next to `destructive`; use them through a primitive's variant, a tone, or a typography variant, never from the app stylesheet. ## The sealed control vocabulary Helm primitives are copied into `libs/ui`, so the set of primitives this repo owns is exactly what that directory ships. Where a primitive covers a native element, use the primitive. Reaching for the bare native element is the drift this rule exists to stop, and it is the one convention worth reading before writing any template. Most primitives are directives you put on the native element, so the markup stays native and accessible and only picks up the Helm styling and behavior. A few have no directive twin and replace the native element outright. Native elements that must carry their primitive directive (any one of the listed attributes satisfies the rule): | native element | primitive attribute | | --- | --- | | `

content.text:
The roster screen is built and `ng build` compiles. The lint pass is clean.

**What's there** (`src/app/heroes/`, the existing `/roster` route target):
- **Filter bar:** a search input (`hlmInput`) and a class filter (`hlm-select` with trigger, value, portal content and items), plus a Recruit button. It wraps with flex.
- **Table:** Hero (avatar, name, ID), Class (outline badge), Power, Status (badge variant per status), Clearance, and Actions (an Edit icon button linking to `/detail/:id`). Empty-state row when nothing matches.
- **Footer:** "N of M heroes" and "sorted by power", as a `tfoot` row.
- **MVVM:** `HeroesViewModel` is component-scoped and holds the search and class state, the filtered and sorted rows, and the `classLabel` and setter methods the template calls. The `Heroes` component is a thin shell.
